title: AI agent architecture
theory: An agent combines a model, instructions, state and tools to achieve a bounded goal. Distinguish deterministic workflows from model-driven decisions. Define a task contract, inputs, outputs, allowed tools, stop conditions and a human escalation path. Start with a local mock model; use a provider only when a budget is approved.
assignment: Design a customer-support agent with a task contract, state diagram and three test conversations. Implement a local rule-based mock and show that it stops or escalates out-of-scope requests.
prompts: Design a bounded customer-support agent with explicit inputs, outputs, permitted tools and stop conditions.
Compare a deterministic workflow and an LLM agent for my use case, including cost and failure modes.
Generate a state-machine specification with a human escalation branch.

title: Tools, APIs and structured outputs
theory: Implement tools as typed functions, not arbitrary command strings. Define JSON input schemas, validate arguments server-side, enforce authorization and handle timeouts. Build a read-only lookup and a simulated write operation behind an approval gate. Keep API keys outside source control. Treat tool responses as untrusted data.
assignment: Build a local agent with two tools: lookup in a sample catalog and prepare a draft action. Validate required fields, reject unexpected values, require explicit approval before simulated writes and log outcomes without secrets.
prompts: Write JSON schemas for a read-only lookup and a draft action with strict validation.
Generate a Python tool registry using an allowlist and mock data, without external API calls.
Create test cases for invalid arguments, timeouts and unauthorized requests.
Review my tool invocation design for prompt injection and accidental side effects.

title: Agent memory, retrieval and knowledge
theory: Separate conversation context from durable memory. Retrieval-augmented generation finds relevant trusted documents, supplies excerpts and asks the model to cite evidence. Use a local collection of sample documents, chunk text, rank matches and return source IDs. Isolate users, set retention rules and ignore instructions embedded in retrieved text.
assignment: Create a local knowledge assistant using five sample documents and keyword retrieval. Return source IDs and an explicit no-answer response when evidence is absent. Test conflicting documents, injected instructions and cross-user isolation.
prompts: Design a retrieval pipeline with source IDs, relevance thresholds and a no-answer state.
Write a local keyword retrieval example using sample documents and standard-library Python.
Create adversarial tests for instructions embedded in retrieved documents.

title: Multi-agent workflows and evaluation
theory: Compose a planner, worker and reviewer with distinct roles and bounded handoffs. Use a deterministic controller to enforce maximum steps and validate outputs. Evaluate against fixtures, compare with a simple baseline, and record success rate, latency, cost estimate and failure categories. Human approval remains required for consequential external actions.
assignment: Build a three-role local workflow with mocked model responses. Run at least ten test cases including malformed outputs, loops and unsupported requests. Report task success, errors, step counts and whether the reviewer catches injected failures.
prompts: Design a planner-worker-reviewer architecture with typed handoffs and a hard stop.
Generate ten evaluation fixtures with expected outputs and failure cases.

Review orchestration logs and suggest three improvements without inventing results.

title: AI agent capstone and deployment
theory: Package the agent as a local service or optional hosted API with authentication, input limits, tool permissions, error handling and observability. Use environment variables for provider configuration, mock mode by default, and explicit budgets before paid requests. Test prompt injection, authorization, outages and rollback. Publish only a sanitized repository and a demo using test data.
assignment: Deliver a working local AI agent with at least two validated tools, evidence retrieval, bounded execution and a human approval gate. Submit source code, README, test results, cost estimate, architecture diagram and a demo. Include at least ten acceptance cases and a rollback plan. Do not use real customer data or paid APIs without authorization.
prompts: Create a deployment checklist for my agent with mock mode, authentication, rate limits and rollback.
Generate a README for a local agent including setup, permissions, budget and known limitations.
